questions.question: In a row, Aman is 20 th from the left and 21 st from the right. How many person are there in this row?
questions.questionHtml: In a row, Aman is 20<sup>th</sup> from the left and 21<sup>st</sup> from the right. How many person are there in this row?
questions.solution:
To find the number of person in the row.

Total number of person = Position of a person from given end + Position of a person from another end - 1

Here, Aman is 20th from the left and 21st from the right.

Therefore, 

Total number of person = 20 + 21 - 1

Total number of person = 40

Therefore, there are 40 person present in a row.

Hence, the correct answer is 40.

questions.questionHtml:
If + means ÷, - means +, x means -, ÷ means x , what will come in place of the ?

{18 × {22 × [60 - 34 + (28 × 11)]} - 62} - 42 = ?
questions.solution:
Decoding the information,

Sign + - x ÷
Means ÷ + - x
 

Given equation: {18 × {22 × [60 - 34 + (28 × 11)]}-62} - 42 = ?

After replacing the sign from left to right and using BODMAS rule, we get  

New Equation: {18 - {22 - [60 + 34 ÷ (28 - 11)]} + 62} + 42 = ?

⇒ {18 - {22 - [60 + 34 ÷ (28 - 11)]} + 62} + 42

⇒ {18 - {22 - [60 + 34 ÷ 17]} + 62} + 42 

⇒ {18 - {22 - [60 + 2]} + 62} + 42 

⇒ {18 - {22 - 62} + 62} + 42 

⇒ {18 - (-40) + 62} + 42 

⇒ {18 + 40 + 36} + 42 

⇒ 94 + 42 

⇒ 136

Hence, the correct answer is "136".

questions.question: What type of forests, consisting of bushes and scrubs, exist in India where the regions receive less than 70 cm rainfall?
questions.questionHtml: What type of forests, consisting of bushes and scrubs, exist in India where the regions receive less than 70 cm rainfall?
questions.solution:
The correct option is Tropical thorn forests.

Key Points

  •  A thorn forest is characterized by dense, scrubland with vegetation as dry subtropical and with warm temperate areas.
  • India has a landmass of 7,12,249 sq. km covered with forest from which 16,491 sq km consist of tropical thorn forest.
  • The tropical thorn forests in India are found in the areas of southwest Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and also in Uttar Pradesh.
  • In the tropical thorn forest trees like – Babool tree, Ber tree and Wild Date Palm, Khair tree, Neem, Khejri tree, Palas tree, etc.
  • There are five types of forests found in India:
    • ​Moist Tropical forest
    • Dry Tropical forest
    • Montane temperate forest
    • Montane sub tropical forest
    • Alpine forest

Additional Information

  •  Moist Tropical forest 
    •  Areas with annual rainfall ranges between 200 and 250 cm.
    •  Found along the Western Coast, in Upper Assam, lower slopes of the eastern Himalaya, Orissa coast and neighbouring hills.
    •  Important plant varieties include Bamboos, Epiphytes, Aini, Semul.
  • Dry Tropical forest
    • ​These forests are generated where average annual rainfall ranges varies from 51 cm to 151.
    • found in Indian Northern Hilly regions and some states of Southern India.
    • Some significant trees of dry tropical forest are sal, acacia, mangoes and bamboo. 
  • Montane temperate forests
    • It takes about 201 cm average annual rainfalls to produce these types of forests.
    • These types of forests are mainly generated in Northern middle Himalayas ranges (1801 to 3001 m) and Southern Niligiri higher Mountain ranges.
    • Some significant trees of montane temperate forest are rhododendrons, ferns, oak, maple etc.
 
  • Montane sub tropical forest
    • ​These types of forests mainly generated in the state of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Meghalaya, Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, etc.
    • Some significant trees of montane sub tropical forest are poonspar, cinnamon, rhododendron, sal, sandan, laburnum, pomegranate, olive.
  • Alpine forest
    • ​They are common in both the main Himalayan regions as well as the barren cold deserts of the Trans Himalaya.
    • ​The vegetation consists mainly of the black juniper, the drooping juniper; honeysuckle and willow are the common trees.

2. UCC refers to the same set of civil laws applicable to all the citizens of India in all the personal matters.

questions.solution: The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India aims to replace personal laws based on scriptures and customs of various religious communities with a common set of laws governing all citizens in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption. The provision for UCC is mentioned under Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, which calls for the state to secure a Uniform Civil Code for all citizens throughout India. The Uniform Civil Code in India Bill, 2020, was introduced in the Lok Sabha, but it was not a private member's bill; it was introduced by the government.

questions.question: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions or writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.questionHtml: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions or writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 32.

Key Points

  • Article 32 of the Indian Constitution provides the right to individuals to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
  • It is known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies" and serves as a guarantor of fundamental rights.
  • The Supreme Court can issue various forms of writs such as Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari under this article.
  • Article 32 is a fundamental right in itself, making it a crucial aspect of the Indian Constitution.
  • Dr. B.R. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the "soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it".

Additional Information

  • Article 29
    • It provides protection of interests of minorities by ensuring that any section of the citizens residing in India having a distinct language, script, or culture have the right to conserve the same.
  • Article 30
    • It grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
  • Article 31
    • Article 31 originally dealt with the right to property, but it was repealed by the 44th Amendment Act in 1978, and the right to property ceased to be a fundamental right.

questions.question: After the Santhal Revolt (1855-56), the Santhal Pargana was created, carving out 5,500 square miles from which of the following districts?
questions.questionHtml: After the Santhal Revolt (1855-56), the Santhal Pargana was created, carving out 5,500 square miles from which of the following districts?
questions.solution: Santhal Pargana was created after the Santhal Revolt (1855-56) by carving out 5,500 square miles from Bhagalpur and Birbhum districts. The rebellion was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, who mobilized ten thousand Santals against British colonists. Santhal Parganas comprised a district of the same name in undivided Bihar state. The Santhals were given land in the foothills of Rajmahal and were to practice plough agriculture and become settled peasants. The demarcated land was called Damin-i-Koh, and Santhal settlements rapidly expanded to 1,473 villages by 1851.

questions.question: Jinasena, a popular scholar of Jainism is associated with which of the following rulers?
questions.questionHtml: Jinasena, a popular scholar of Jainism is associated with which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​Amoghavarsha I.

Key Points

  • ​Jinasena (c. 9th century CE) was a monk and scholar in the Digambara tradition of Jainism.
    • He was patronized by the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I.
    • He wrote Sanskrit philosophical treatises and poetry with the support of the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I.
    • Jinasena composed Parsvabhudaya, a biography of Parsva in verses.
  • Amoghavarsha I:
    • Amoghavarsha I (800–878) C.E. was a Rashtrakuta king, the greatest ruler of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, and one of the great kings of India. 
    • He ruled for a long period of 64 years.
    • He had lost control over Malwa and Gangavadi.
    • Yet his reign was popular for cultural development.
    • He was a follower of Jainism.
      • Jinasena was his chief preceptor.
    • He was also a patron of letters and he himself wrote the famous Kannada work, Kavirajamarga.
    • He had also built the Rashtrakuta capital, the city of Malkhed or Manyakheda.
    •  Amoghavarsha apparently renounced his throne and became a disciple of Jinasena in the early 9th century.

Additional Information

  • Krishna I (reign 756–774 CE), an uncle of Dantidurga, took charge of the growing Rashtrakuta Empire by defeating the last Badami Chalukya ruler Kirtivarman II in 757.
    • Krishna I, built the rock temple of Kailasa at Ellora (designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1983)
  • Dhruva Dharavarsha (ruled 780–793 CE) was one of the most notable rulers of the Rashtrakuta Empire. He ascended the throne after replacing his elder brother Govinda II. 
    • He expanded the empire to such an extent that it encompassed all of the territories between the Kaveri River and Central India.
  • Krishna III whose Kannada name was Kannara (r. 939 – 967 C.E.) was the last great warrior and able monarch of the Rashtrakuta dynasty of Manyakheta.
    • He was a shrewd administrator and skilful military campaigner.
    • He patronised the famous Kannada poet Sri Ponna, who wrote Shanti Purana.

questions.question: With reference to the ‘Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO)’, consider the following statements: 1. It is an oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon which affects weather activities most prominent over the Indian and Pacific Oceans. 2. Presence of Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) over the Pacific Ocean along with an El Nino is detrimental to Monsoon rains. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionHtml:
With reference to the ‘Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO)’, consider the following statements: 

1. It is an oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon which affects weather activities most prominent over the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

2. Presence of Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) over the Pacific Ocean along with an El Nino is detrimental to Monsoon rains.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

 Madden-Julian Oscillation:

  • The Madden–Julian Oscillation (MJO), as it’s called, is a moving band of rain clouds that travels around the globe-spanning 12,000–20,000 km across the tropical oceans. 
  • There can be multiple MJO events within a season, and so the MJO is best described as intra-seasonal tropical climate variability.
  • The surface and upper-atmosphere structure of the MJO for a period when the enhanced convective phase (thunderstorm cloud) is centred across the Indian Ocean and the suppressed convective phase is centred over the west-central Pacific Ocean.
  • The entire system shifts eastward over time, eventually circling the globe and returning to its point of origin. 
  • Thus, It is an oceanic-atmospheric phenomenon which affects weather activities most prominent over the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • Effects of MJO on global weather phenomenon:
    • The presence of Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) over the Pacific Ocean along with an El Nino is detrimental to Monsoon rains. It can modulate the timing and strength of monsoons. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
    • It Influences tropical cyclone numbers and strength in nearly all ocean basins.
    • It can result in jet stream changes that can lead to cold air outbreaks, extreme heat events, and flooding rains over the United States and North America.

questions.question: In medieval India, "Bandobast system and Dahsala System" were known as the land revenue systems introduced by whom among the following?
questions.questionHtml: In medieval India, "Bandobast system and Dahsala System" were known as the land revenue systems introduced by whom among the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Akbar and Todar Mal

Important Points

  • Bandobast system and Dahsala System or Zabti System (land revenue system) were introduced by Raja Todarmal, who was then the finance minister of Akbar. Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.
  • In this system, the average produce of ten years was derived.
  • One-third of this average produce was fixed in Rupees per Bigha and fixed as a share of the state (Mal).
  • Rest two third share was left to the cultivators (Kharaj).
  • The state demand in kind was given in maunds; but for the conversion of the state demand from kind to cash, a separate schedule of cash revenue rates for various crops was fixed, which were called as Dastur-i-Amal.
  • Each revenue circle had a separate schedule of dastur-i-amal for various crops.
  • Thus the peasant was required to pay on the basis of local produce as well as local prices.
  • The main features of the Zabti system as it finally came into operation under Akbar were:
    • i) Land was measured and assessed
    • ii) Crops were surveyed
    • iii)One-third of the average produce was fixed as the state's share
    • iv)Cash revenue rates were fixed
    • v)The revenue was collected in cash
    • vi) all the collection was made in cash.

Pyroclastic material and ashes accumulates in the vicinity of the vent openings leading to formation of layers. Above statements describes which of the following Volcanoes?

2. Pyroclastic material and ashes accumulates in the vicinity of the vent openings leading to formation of layers.

Above statements describes which of the following Volcanoes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Composite Volcanoes

Key Points

Volcanoes:

  • ​Volcanoes are classified on the basis of the nature of eruption and the form developed at the surface.
  • Major types of volcanoes are as follows:
    • Shield Volcanoes
      • ​Barring the basalt flows, the shield volcanoes are the largest of all the volcanoes on the earth.
      • The Hawaiian volcanoes are the most famous examples.
    • Caldera:
      • ​These are the most explosive of the earth’s volcanoes.
      • They are usually so explosive that when they erupt they tend to collapse on themselves rather than building any tall structure.
    • Composite Volcanoes:
      • ​These volcanoes are characterised by eruptions of cooler and more viscous lavas than basalt. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
      • These volcanoes often result in explosive eruptions.
      • Along with lava, large quantities of pyroclastic material and ashes find their way to the ground. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
        • This material accumulates in the vicinity of the vent openings leading to the formation of layers, and this makes the mounts appear as composite volcanoes.
    • Flood Basalt Provinces
      • ​These volcanoes outpour highly fluid lava that flows for long distances.
      • The Deccan Traps from India, presently covering most of the Maharashtra plateau, are a much larger flood basalt province.

questions.question: Rs 30000 became Rs 42000 in 8 years. If the investment was made on simple interest, what was the rate on simple interest offered per annum?
questions.questionHtml: Rs 30000 became Rs 42000 in 8 years. If the investment was made on simple interest, what was the rate on simple interest offered per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total interest percentage over 8 years = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Total Interest % = (12,000 ÷ 30,000) × 100 = 40%

Annual Rate of Interest = Total % ÷ Time

Annual Rate = 40% ÷ 8 = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹30,000

Amount (A) = ₹42,000

Time (T) = 8 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

Rate (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

Calculations:

⇒ SI = 42,000 − 30,000

⇒ SI = ₹12,000

⇒ R = (12,000 × 100) ÷ (30,000 × 8)

⇒ R = 1,200,000 ÷ 240,000

⇒ R = 120 ÷ 24

⇒ R = 5%

∴ The correct answer is 5%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal.

Sum and Amount Relation

The total Amount after T years is given by A = P × (1 + RT/100).

SI vs CI Difference

For the first year (if compounded annually), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always equal.

questions.question: The mean of the marks obtained by a child in five subjects is 74. He scored 70, 75 and 80 marks in three of the subjects. What is the mean of the marks obtained by the child in the remaining two subjects?
questions.questionHtml: The mean of the marks obtained by a child in five subjects is 74. He scored 70, 75 and 80 marks in three of the subjects. What is the mean of the marks obtained by the child in the remaining two subjects?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Overall Mean of 5 subjects = 74.

Net deviation of 3 given subjects: (70−74) + (75−74) + (80−74) = −4 + 1 + 6 = +3.

To maintain the average, total deviation for remaining 2 subjects must be −3.

Average deviation for remaining 2 subjects = −3 ÷ 2 = −1.5.

Required Mean = 74 − 1.5 = 72.5.

∴ The correct answer is 72.5 marks.

Alternate Method

Given: The mean marks of 5 subjects is 74. Marks in 3 subjects are 70, 75, and 80.

Formula Used: Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

⇒ Total marks in 5 subjects = Mean × 5 = 74 × 5 = 370.

⇒ Sum of marks in 3 subjects = 70 + 75 + 80 = 225.

⇒ Sum of marks in remaining 2 subjects = 370 − 225 = 145.

⇒ Mean of remaining 2 subjects = 145 ÷ 2 = 72.5.

∴ The correct answer is 72.5 marks.

Additional Information

Arithmetic Mean Properties

The sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. Σ(xi − Mean) = 0.

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with averages A1 and A2 and sizes n1 and n2, the combined average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Impact of Constant on Mean

If every observation is increased or decreased by a constant k, the mean also increases or decreases by k.

questions.question: If the number 22144 is divided in the ratio \(\frac{1}{3}\) ∶ \(\frac{3}{5}\) ∶ \(\frac{5}{7}\) , the difference between the largest and smallest part is:
questions.questionHtml: If the number 22144 is divided in the ratio \(\frac{1}{3}\) ∶ \(\frac{3}{5}\) ∶ \(\frac{5}{7}\), the difference between the largest and smallest part is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simplify Ratio by multiplying by LCM(3, 5, 7) = 105: (1/3 × 105) : (3/5 × 105) : (5/7 × 105) = 35 : 63 : 75.

Total units = 35 + 63 + 75 = 173 units.

Total Value = 22144 ⇒ 1 unit = 22144 ÷ 173 = 128.

Difference between Largest (75) and Smallest (35) = 75 − 35 = 40 units.

Required Difference = 40 × 128 = 5120.

∴ The correct answer is 5120.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Number = 22144

Ratio = 1/3 : 3/5 : 5/7

Formula Used:

Value of a part = (Ratio of part ÷ Sum of ratios) × Total Value

Calculations:

⇒ Simplifying the ratio by finding LCM of 3, 5, and 7:

⇒ LCM(3, 5, 7) = 105

⇒ New Ratio = (1/3 × 105) : (3/5 × 105) : (5/7 × 105) = 35 : 63 : 75

⇒ Let the three parts be 35x, 63x, and 75x

⇒ 35x + 63x + 75x = 22144

⇒ 173x = 22144

⇒ x = 22144 ÷ 173 = 128

⇒ Smallest part = 35x = 35 × 128 = 4480

⇒ Largest part = 75x = 75 × 128 = 9600

⇒ Required Difference = 9600 − 4480 = 5120

∴ The correct answer is 5120.

Additional Information

Ratio Normalization

To convert a fractional ratio a/b : c/d : e/f into an integer ratio, multiply each term by the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators (b, d, f).

Direct Difference Calculation

Instead of calculating individual parts, the difference can be found directly using the formula: Difference = (Difference in ratio parts ÷ Sum of ratio parts) × Total Value.

Property of Proportion

If a : b : c is the ratio of three quantities whose sum is S, then the parts are S × a/(a+b+c), S × b/(a+b+c), and S × c/(a+b+c).

questions.question: The perimeters of two squares are 52 cm and 20 cm. Find the perimeter of a third square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of these two squares.
questions.questionHtml: The perimeters of two squares are 52 cm and 20 cm. Find the perimeter of a third square whose area is equal to the difference of the areas of these two squares.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sides of the given squares are 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm and 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm.

According to the question, Area3 = Area1 − Area2

Side of the 3rd square = √(132 − 52) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm.

Perimeter of the 3rd square = 4 × 12 = 48 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of 1st square = 52 cm

Perimeter of 2nd square = 20 cm

Formula Used:

Perimeter of a square = 4 × Side

Area of a square = Side2

Calculations:

⇒ Side of 1st square (a1) = 52 ÷ 4 = 13 cm

⇒ Area of 1st square (A1) = 132 = 169 cm2

⇒ Side of 2nd square (a2) = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm

⇒ Area of 2nd square (A2) = 52 = 25 cm2

⇒ Area of 3rd square (A3) = A1 − A2

⇒ A3 = 169 − 25 = 144 cm2

⇒ Side of 3rd square (a3) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Perimeter of 3rd square = 4 × 12 = 48 cm

∴ The correct answer is 48 cm.

Additional Information

Diagonal of a Square

The length of the diagonal is given by d = a√2, where 'a' is the side length of the square.

Area using Perimeter

The area can be found directly from the perimeter using the formula Area = (P ÷ 4)2.

questions.question: Two friends, one of whom is thrice as efficient as the other, working together, can complete a work in 6 days. In how many days will the less efficient among the two be able to complete twice the quantum of work?
questions.questionHtml: Two friends, one of whom is thrice as efficient as the other, working together, can complete a work in 6 days. In how many days will the less efficient among the two be able to complete twice the quantum of work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Efficiency (A : B) = 3 : 1

Combined Efficiency = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

Total Work = 4 units/day × 6 days = 24 units

Twice the quantum of work = 24 × 2 = 48 units

Time for less efficient person = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 days

∴ The correct answer is 48 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by both working together = 6 days

Efficiency of one friend = 3 × Efficiency of the other

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
More Efficient (A) 8 24 3
Less Efficient (B) 24 1

Calculations:

⇒ Let efficiency of less efficient friend B = 1 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of friend A = 3 × 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Combined Efficiency = 1 + 3 = 4 units/day

⇒ Total Work = 4 × 6 = 24 units

⇒ Twice the work = 2 × 24 = 48 units

⇒ Time taken by B = 48 ÷ 1 = 48 days

∴ The correct answer is 48 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relation

The time taken to complete a specific task is inversely proportional to the efficiency of the person. Formula: E1 × T1 = E2 × T2.

Work and Wages

If individuals work for the same amount of time, the wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same logic applies where efficiency is the rate of flow. Total capacity of the tank = Combined rate × Total filling time.

questions.question: A can do a certain work in 18 days. B is 25% less efficient than A. A alone worked for a few days and then, B joined him. Both worked together till the completion of the work. The entire work got completed in 12 days. For how many days did A and B work together?
questions.questionHtml: A can do a certain work in 18 days. B is 25% less efficient than A. A alone worked for a few days and then, B joined him. Both worked together till the completion of the work. The entire work got completed in 12 days. For how many days did A and B work together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio A : B = 100 : 75 = 4 : 3

Total Work = A's efficiency × A's time = 4 × 18 = 72 units

A worked for the entire 12 days, so work done by A = 12 × 4 = 48 units

Remaining work done by B = 72 − 48 = 24 units

Number of days B worked (and worked with A) = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

∴ The correct answer is 8 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A = 18 days

Efficiency of B = 25% less than A

Total completion time = 12 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 18 72 4
B 24 3

Calculations:

⇒ Let A's efficiency be 4 units/day.

⇒ B's efficiency = 4 − (25% of 4) = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day.

⇒ Total work = 18 × 4 = 72 units.

⇒ Let A and B work together for 'x' days.

⇒ This means A worked for 12 days and B worked for 'x' days.

⇒ (12 × 4) + (x × 3) = 72

⇒ 48 + 3x = 72

⇒ 3x = 72 − 48

⇒ 3x = 24

⇒ x = 8 days

∴ The correct answer is 8 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the efficiency ratio of A:B is x:y, then the time ratio is y:x.

Combined Work Principle

When individuals work together, their efficiencies (work per unit time) are additive: Total Efficiency = E1 + E2 + ... + En.

Work and Wages

Wages are generally distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person, which depends on both their individual efficiency and the time they worked.

questions.question: The least number of square tiles required to pave the ceiling of a room 525 centimetre long and 378 centimetre broad is:
questions.questionHtml: The least number of square tiles required to pave the ceiling of a room 525 centimetre long and 378 centimetre broad is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For the least number of square tiles, we must maximize the side of each tile.

Side of square tile = HCF(525, 378).

Prime factors: 525 = 3 × 52 × 7 and 378 = 2 × 33 × 7.

HCF = 3 × 7 = 21 cm.

Number of tiles = (525 ÷ 21) × (378 ÷ 21) = 25 × 18 = 450.

∴ The correct answer is 450 tiles.

Alternate Method

Given: Length of the ceiling = 525 cm, Breadth of the ceiling = 378 cm.

Formula Used:

Side of the largest square tile = HCF(Length, Breadth)

Number of tiles = (Area of Ceiling) ÷ (Area of one square tile)

Calculations:

⇒ Prime factorization of 525 = 3 × 5 × 5 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 378 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 7

⇒ HCF(525, 378) = 3 × 7 = 21 cm

⇒ Area of the ceiling = 525 × 378 cm2

⇒ Area of one square tile = 21 × 21 cm2

⇒ Total tiles required = (525 × 378) ÷ (21 × 21)

⇒ Total tiles required = 25 × 18 = 450

∴ The correct answer is 450 tiles.

Additional Information

HCF Application

HCF is used to find the largest identical size that can divide two or more dimensions perfectly without leaving any remainder.

Area Comparison

The number of units required to fill a surface is always the Total Area divided by the Unit Area.

LCM in Tiling

While HCF finds the tile size for a fixed room, LCM is used to find the smallest square room that can be paved using fixed-size rectangular tiles.

questions.question: In a circle of radius 37 cm, two parallel chords of length 70 cm and 24 cm are drawn. If both chords are on the same side of the centre. Then the distance between the chords is
questions.questionHtml: In a circle of radius 37 cm, two parallel chords of length 70 cm and 24 cm are drawn. If both chords are on the same side of the centre. Then the distance between the chords is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the Pythagorean triplet for the given radius 37 cm: 122 + 352 = 372.

For Chord 1 (70 cm), half-length = 35 cm → Distance from center d1 = 12 cm.

For Chord 2 (24 cm), half-length = 12 cm → Distance from center d2 = 35 cm.

Since both chords are on the same side of the centre, the distance between them is the difference of their distances from the centre.

Distance = d2 − d1 = 35 cm − 12 cm = 23 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 23 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle (r) = 37 cm

Length of Chord 1 (AB) = 70 cm

Length of Chord 2 (CD) = 24 cm

Formula Used:

The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord. If d is the distance of a chord of length L from the centre of a circle with radius r, then: d = √(r2 − (L/2)2)

Calculations:

⇒ Half-length of Chord 1 (a) = 70 ÷ 2 = 35 cm

⇒ Distance of Chord 1 from centre (d1) = √(372 − 352)

⇒ d1 = √(1369 − 1225) = √144 = 12 cm

⇒ Half-length of Chord 2 (b) = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Distance of Chord 2 from centre (d2) = √(372 − 122)

⇒ d2 = √(1369 − 144) = √1225 = 35 cm

⇒ Distance between chords = d2 − d1 (since both are on the same side)

⇒ Distance = 35 cm − 12 cm = 23 cm

∴ The correct answer is 23 cm.

Additional Information

Chord Distance Rule

If parallel chords are on opposite sides of the center, the distance between them is the sum of their distances from the center (d1 + d2).

Perpendicular Bisector

A line drawn from the centre of a circle that is perpendicular to a chord always bisects that chord into two equal segments.

Length-Distance Inverse Relation

The longer the chord, the closer it is to the centre of the circle.

questions.question: There are 17 consecutive odd numbers. If the average of first 11 numbers is X, then what is the average of last 6 numbers?
questions.questionHtml: There are 17 consecutive odd numbers. If the average of first 11 numbers is X, then what is the average of last 6 numbers?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average of 11 consecutive odd numbers is the middle term, which is the 6th term = X.

The last 6 numbers are the 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th, and 17th terms.

Average of these 6 numbers is the mid-point between the 14th and 15th terms (i.e., 14.5th position).

Difference in positions = 14.5 − 6 = 8.5 steps.

Since the difference between consecutive odd numbers is 2, the total increase = 8.5 × 2 = 17.

∴ The correct answer is X + 17.

Alternate Method

Given: Total numbers = 17, Average of first 11 = X.

Formula: For an Arithmetic Progression (AP), Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

⇒ Let the 17 numbers be a1, a2, ..., a17 with common difference d = 2.

⇒ Average of first 11 numbers = a6 = X.

⇒ 12th number (a12) = a6 + (12 − 6) × 2 = X + 6 × 2 = X + 12.

⇒ 17th number (a17) = a6 + (17 − 6) × 2 = X + 11 × 2 = X + 22.

⇒ Average of last 6 numbers (from a12 to a17) = (a12 + a17) ÷ 2.

⇒ Average = (X + 12 + X + 22) ÷ 2 = (2X + 34) ÷ 2.

⇒ Average = X + 17.

∴ The correct answer is X + 17.

Additional Information

Consecutive Numbers Property

For any odd number of terms in an AP, the average is exactly the middle term.

Common Difference

For consecutive odd or consecutive even numbers, the common difference (d) is always 2.

Average of AP

The average of any subset of an AP is the arithmetic mean of its first and last terms: (a + l) ÷ 2.

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 16% if he allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article. What will be the profit percent earned by the shopkeeper if he sold the article at its marked price?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 16% if he allows a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article. What will be the profit percent earned by the shopkeeper if he sold the article at its marked price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP) = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP : MP = (100 − 20) : (100 + 16) = 80 : 116

If the article is sold at Marked Price, Profit = 116 − 80 = 36 units

Profit% = (36 ÷ 80) × 100 = 45%

∴ The correct answer is 45%.

Alternate Method

Given: Profit = 16%, Discount = 20%.

Formula used: MP = [SP ÷ (100 − Discount%)] × 100; Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = ₹100

⇒ Since Profit is 16%, Selling Price (SP) = 116% of 100 = ₹116

⇒ This SP is achieved after a 20% Discount on Marked Price (MP)

⇒ 80% of MP = ₹116

⇒ MP = (116 × 100) ÷ 80 = 1.45 × 100 = ₹145

⇒ If sold at MP, new SP = ₹145

⇒ New Profit = 145 − 100 = ₹45

⇒ Profit% = (45 ÷ 100) × 100 = 45%

∴ The correct answer is 45%.

Additional Information

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between CP and MP is given by CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%), where D is discount and P is profit.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % is the percentage by which MP is higher than CP: Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d1 and d2 are given, the effective discount is d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100.

questions.question: If gain 124% by selling an item for Rs. 1,232, then what would be my gain or loss percentage if I sell it for Rs. 572?
questions.questionHtml: If gain 124% by selling an item for Rs. 1,232, then what would be my gain or loss percentage if I sell it for Rs. 572?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the ratio of percentages: (100 + 124)% corresponds to ₹1,232.

⇒ 224% → 1232

⇒ 1% → 1232 ÷ 224 = 5.5

⇒ New Percentage for ₹572 ⇒ 572 ÷ 5.5 = 104%

⇒ Gain Percentage = 104% − 100% = 4% gain.

∴ The correct answer is 4% gain.

Alternate Method

Given: First Selling Price (SP1) = ₹1,232, Profit = 124%, Second Selling Price (SP2) = ₹572.

Formula Used: Cost Price (CP) = [SP ÷ (100 + Profit%)] × 100; Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = [1232 ÷ (100 + 124)] × 100

⇒ CP = (1232 ÷ 224) × 100

⇒ CP = 5.5 × 100 = ₹550

⇒ Profit on selling at ₹572 = 572 − 550 = ₹22

⇒ Profit Percentage = (22 ÷ 550) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 25) × 100 = 4%

∴ The correct answer is 4% gain.

Additional Information

Basic Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit = Selling Price − Cost Price; Loss = Cost Price − Selling Price.

Percentage Calculation

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

Selling Price for Loss

If there is a loss of L%, then SP = CP × (100 − L) ÷ 100.

questions.question: If Manoj cycles at 12 kmph instead of 10 kmph, he would have cycled 15 km more. What is the actual distance cycled by him?
questions.questionHtml: If Manoj cycles at 12 kmph instead of 10 kmph, he would have cycled 15 km more. What is the actual distance cycled by him?
questions.solution:
Distance travelled when person walks at 10 kmph, 10 = x / t⇒ x = 10t.

Distance travelled when person walks at 12 kmph, 12 = (x + 15) / t ⇒ x + 15 = 12t ⇒ 10t + 15 = 12t ⇒ 2t = 15 ⇒t = 7.5 hours.

Actual distance travelled by him ⇒ x = 10t = 10(7.5) = 75 km.

questions.question: The admission to a college is increased by 4% per year, If there is an additional 1% increase in the admission to the college as per of management quota. Find the percentage increase in the admission after 2 years.
questions.questionHtml: The admission to a college is increased by 4% per year, If there is an additional 1% increase in the admission to the college as per of management quota. Find the percentage increase in the admission after 2 years.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total annual growth rate = 4% (regular) + 1% (quota) = 5%.

For two successive years, net percentage increase = x + y + (x × y)/100.

Net Increase = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = 10 + 25/100 = 10.25%.

∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.

Alternate Method

Given: Annual increase = 4%, Management quota increase = 1%, Time = 2 years.

Let the initial admission be 100 units.

⇒ Effective annual growth rate = 4% + 1% = 5%

⇒ Admission after 1st year = 100 + (5% of 100) = 100 + 5 = 105

⇒ Admission after 2nd year = 105 + (5% of 105)

⇒ Admission after 2nd year = 105 + 5.25 = 110.25

⇒ Net percentage increase = (Final value − Initial value) / Initial value × 100

⇒ Net increase = (110.25 − 100) / 100 × 100 = 10.25%

∴ The correct answer is 10.25%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by x% and then by y% successively, the net change is given by the formula: [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Compound Growth Formula

For annual growth over 'n' years at rate 'r', the final amount A is calculated as: A = P(1 + r/100)n, where P is the initial value.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d1% and d2% are given, the equivalent single discount is [d1 + d2 − (d1 × d2)/100]%.

questions.question: A, B and C share the profit in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 7. If the average gain is Rs. 8000, then B's share is ?
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C share the profit in the ratio of 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 7. If the average gain is Rs. 8000, then B's share is ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average of the ratio parts (2, 3, 7) = (2 + 3 + 7) ÷ 3 = 4 units.

Given Average Gain = ₹8000, so 4 units = ₹8000.

1 unit = 8000 ÷ 4 = ₹2000.

B's share (3 units) = 3 × 2000 = ₹6000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Alternate Method

Given: Ratio of profit sharing A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 7 and the Average Gain = ₹8000.

Formula: Total Profit = Average Profit × Number of Partners.

⇒ Total profit gain = Average gain × 3

⇒ Total Profit = 8000 × 3 = ₹24,000

⇒ Let the shares of A, B, and C be 2x, 3x, and 7x respectively.

⇒ Total units = 2x + 3x + 7x = 12x

⇒ 12x = 24000

⇒ x = 24000 ÷ 12 = 2000

⇒ B's share = 3x = 3 × 2000 = ₹6,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Additional Information

Profit Sharing in Partnership

In a business, Profit Ratio is directly proportional to the product of Investment and Time. If time is equal, profit is shared in the ratio of capital.

Average and Total Sum

Total Sum = Average × Number of terms. Always convert average to total sum before distributing it using ratios.

Ratio Distribution

To find an individual part: (Individual Ratio Part ÷ Sum of all Ratio Parts) × Total Value.

questions.question: Divide ₹18,400 among 6 men, 13 women and 6 boys such that the ratio of the shares of a man, a women and a boy is 5 : 4 : 3. How much money will each boy receive?
questions.questionHtml: Divide ₹18,400 among 6 men, 13 women and 6 boys such that the ratio of the shares of a man, a women and a boy is 5 : 4 : 3. How much money will each boy receive?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total units = (6 men × 5) + (13 women × 4) + (6 boys × 3)

Total units = 30 + 52 + 18 = 100 units

100 units = ₹18,400 → 1 unit = ₹184

Individual share of each boy = 3 units = 3 × 184 = ₹552

∴ The correct answer is ₹552.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount to be divided = ₹18,400

Ratio of individual shares (Man : Woman : Boy) = 5 : 4 : 3

Number of people: 6 men, 13 women, and 6 boys

Formula Used:

Total Share of a group = Number of individuals × Individual share ratio

Calculations:

⇒ Let the individual share of a man, a woman, and a boy be 5x, 4x, and 3x respectively.

⇒ Total share of 6 men = 6 × 5x = 30x

⇒ Total share of 13 women = 13 × 4x = 52x

⇒ Total share of 6 boys = 6 × 3x = 18x

⇒ Total sum = 30x + 52x + 18x = 100x

⇒ 100x = 18400

⇒ x = 184

⇒ Share of each boy = 3x = 3 × 184 = ₹552

∴ The correct answer is ₹552.

Additional Information

Ratio and Proportion

If a : b = c : d, then the product of extremes equals the product of means (a × d = b × c).

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios (a : b) and (c : d) is (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

Duplicate ratio of a : b is a2 : b2, while the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

questions.question: The numerator of a fraction is 4 less than its denominator. If the numerator is decreased by 2 and denominator is increased by 1, then the denominator becomes 8 times the numerator, find the fraction.
questions.questionHtml: The numerator of a fraction is 4 less than its denominator. If the numerator is decreased by 2 and denominator is increased by 1, then the denominator becomes 8 times the numerator, find the fraction.
questions.solution:
Let numerator be x and denominator be (x + 4)

questions.question: Find the fourth proportional to 19, 23 and 38.
questions.questionHtml: Find the fourth proportional to 19, 23 and 38.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the relationship can be seen between terms.

Observe the first and third terms: 19 → 38 (multiplied by 2).

Apply the same multiplier to the second term to find the fourth term.

Fourth proportional = 23 × 2 = 46.

∴ The correct answer is 46.

Alternate Method

Given: First term (a) = 19, Second term (b) = 23, Third term (c) = 38.

Formula Used: If a, b, c, and d are in proportion, then a/b = c/d or Product of Extremes = Product of Means (a × d = b × c).

Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 19 : 23 :: 38 : x

⇒ 19/23 = 38/x

⇒ x = (23 × 38) / 19

⇒ x = 23 × 2

⇒ x = 46

∴ The correct answer is 46.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then the third proportional c = b2 / a.

Invertendo Property

If a : b = c : d, then b : a = d : c. This is used to simplify ratios by reciprocating both sides.

Alternendo Property

If a : b = c : d, then a : c = b : d. This allows swapping the internal terms of the proportion.

questions.question: What is the value of (a - b) 3 - a 3 + b 3 ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of (a - b)<sup>3</sup> - a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup>?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Expand the expression using the algebraic identity: (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b).

Substitute this expansion into the given expression: [a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b)] − a3 + b3.

Cancel the identical terms with opposite signs: a3 − a3 = 0 and −b3 + b3 = 0.

The remaining term is −3ab(a − b).

∴ The correct answer is -3ab(a - b).

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = (a − b)3 − a3 + b3

Formula Used:

The standard cubic expansion identity is: (x − y)3 = x3 − 3x2y + 3xy2 − y3

This can also be written as: (x − y)3 = x3 − y3 − 3xy(x − y)

Calculations:

⇒ (a − b)3 − a3 + b3

⇒ [a3 − 3a2b + 3ab2 − b3] − a3 + b3

⇒ a3 − a3 − b3 + b3 − 3a2b + 3ab2

⇒ 0 + 0 − 3a2b + 3ab2

⇒ −3ab(a − b)

∴ The correct answer is -3ab(a - b).

Additional Information

Cubical Identity (Sum)

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b) or a3 + 3a2b + 3ab2 + b3.

Difference of Cubes

a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).

Sum of Cubes

a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2).
